correctness.rationale: Reversing the labels makes rate k correspond to increasing rank n−k+1, so a fixed point is equivalent to k−1 clocks exceeding its own. The exponential race and conditioning yield the stated integral. For any realized Bernoulli vector, only k=S or k=S+1 can contribute, giving the uniform logarithmic domination and the bounded contribution from t<1/n; the geometric-series estimate makes the t≥1 tail integrable. In the scaling window t→0, nt→∞, geometric sums give tm→1 and tv→1/2 for the exceedance mean and variance. The characteristic-function bound follows by taking the square root of 1−4p(1−p)sin²(θ/2) for each Bernoulli factor and multiplying. Fourier inversion for adjacent masses introduces |1−exp(iθ)|≤|θ|, giving π/(4V), uniform after deleting any one summand since V≥v−1/4. Hence the deletion changes the total mass over k within M sqrt(v) of m by O(M/sqrt(v)). The comparison masses sum to P(S<n)=1−o(1) because m/n→0; Chebyshev and the two-index identity bound the two exterior masses by (1+o(1))/M² and (2+o(1))/M². The normalized weight tk exp(−tk) tends uniformly to 1/e on each such band, and is bounded globally by 1/e. Sending M to infinity and using t=n^(−u) with dominated convergence gives the stated limit along every n. A fresh rational recursion over remaining-label subsets, drawing label j with weight (n−j+1) divided by the remaining total and crediting a hit exactly at position n−|subset|+1=j, reproduced all seven recorded expectations (last 8823199676/5019589575).
residual_risks: Finite checks do not prove the asymptotic; the preceding argument does. The frozen script was not executed. No variance or distributional conclusion is part of correctness here.

evidence: The singular case is discussed as open for fixed-point distribution in §5.2. Mukherjee requires regular positive continuous density with local control, Paguyo treats uniform double-coset sampling, and Borga–Dubach treat LIS. Long instead also states a stronger local Poisson point-process limit on log-terminal windows whose centers tend to infinity and are o(n).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The first four primary comparisons do not imply the leading singular mean. Long covers it directly, not by claiming that a local Poisson limit alone yields a globally integrated mean.

originality.rationale: Christopher D. Long's Sukhatme Fixed Points and the Terminal Poisson Process states this exact leading mean under exactly the same weights as Theorem 3.5, and supplies a proof via a uniform one-point terminal saddle estimate and a harmonic sum. The publicly readable PDF at committing revision 32b0620 contains that theorem; the repository history dates the addition to 2026-10-12, before the frozen record. The identity of theorem, weights and statistic is decisive, not the keyword hit or the incompletely retrievable older extraction provenance.
